== Chimyō Gongen ==
'''Chimyō Gongen''' (智明権現) is a {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}} blending {{ill|Mountain worship|fa|کوه‌پرستی|ja|山岳信仰|ko|산악신앙|simple|Mountain worship|zh|山岳信仰|qid=Q93697439|lt=mountain worship}} and {{ill|Shugendō|en|Shugendō|qid=Q1483875|lt=Shugendō}} from {{ill|Mount Daisen|en|Mount Daisen|qid=Q715498|lt=Mount Daisen}}. It is considered the {{ill|Honji suijaku|en|Honji suijaku|qid=Q3080781|lt=Honji Buddha}} (original Buddha) manifestation of {{ill|Kṣitigarbha|en|Kṣitigarbha|qid=Q604687|lt=Jizō Bosatsu}}. Before the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|en|Haibutsu kishaku|qid=Q702298|lt=Haibutsu kishaku}} (anti-Buddhist movement), Chimyō Gongen was enshrined in various shrines nationwide, having been {{ill|Bunrei|es|Bunrei|fr|Bunrei|id|Bunrei|ja|分霊|simple|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=Enshrinement}} from {{ill|Daisen-ji|en|Daisen-ji|qid=Q3012163|lt=Daisen-ji}} in {{ill|Hōki Province|en|Hōki Province|qid=Q1053703|lt=Hōki Province}}. It is also known as Daichimyō Gongen (大智明権現), Daichimyō Daigongen (大智明大権現), Daisen Chimyō Daigongen (大山智明大権現), and Daisen Chimyō Gongen (大仙智明大権現).
== Overview ==
Mount Daisen, regarded as a sacred body in ancient mountain worship, was identified as a manifestation of Jizō Bosatsu. According to legend, {{ill|Shunpō|ja|俊方}} from {{ill|Tamatsukuri, Izumo Province|ja|Izumo Province 玉造}} founded Daisen-ji during the {{ill|Yōrō|de|Yōrō (Ära)|es|Yōrō|fa|یورو (دوره)|fr|Ère Yōrō|ia|Yoro|id|Yōrō|it|Yōrō (era)|ja|養老|ko|요로 (연호)|ru|Ёро (нэнго)|simple|Yōrō|sr|Јоро|tr|Yōrō|uk|Йоро (ненґо)|zh|養老 (日本)|zh_yue|養老|qid=Q1373061|lt=Yōrō era}} (717–724 CE) period.<ref name="daisenji">[http://www.daisenji.jp/index.php?id=9 Tendaishū Bekkaku Honzan Kakuban-san Daisen-ji - Temple Overview]</ref> The {{ill|Senchūshō|ja|選集抄}} recounts how Shunpō accidentally shot what he believed was a deer but turned out to be Jizō Bosatsu. Overcome with remorse, he became a monk, took the name Konren, and established a hermitage to enshrine Jizō Bosatsu. Similar stories are found in the {{ill|Daisen-ji Engi|ja|大山寺縁起|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97184197}}.<ref name="daisenji"/>
In {{ill|Jingo-keiun|en|Jingo-keiun|qid=Q1373049|lt=Jingo-keiun}} 1 (767 CE), {{ill|Empress Kōken|ar|الإمبراطورة شوتوكو|azb|امپراتریس کوکن|bcl|Emperatris Kōken|be|Імператрыца Кокэн|ca|Shōtoku|cs|Kóken|de|Kōken|es|Kōken Tennō|eu|Kōken enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس کوکن|fi|Kōken|fr|Kōken|hak|Kōken Thiên-fòng|hu|Kóken japán császárnő|id|Maharani Kōken|it|Kōken|ja|孝謙天皇|ko|고켄 천황|nl|Koken (keizerin)|no|Kōken|pl|Shōtoku (cesarzowa)|pt|Shotoku|ru|Императрица Кокэн|sh|Carica Kōken|sl|Cesarica Koken|sv|Koken (kejsarinna)|ta|பேரரசி கோகன்|th|จักรพรรดินีโคเก็ง|tl|Emperatris Kōken|tr|Kōken (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператор Кокен|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōken|zh|孝谦天皇|zh_classical|孝謙天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôken Thian-hông|qid=Q232955}} conferred the honorary title of Daichimyō Daigongen on the Jizō Bosatsu of Mount Daisen as part of syncretic practices.<ref name="daisenji"/> During the medieval period, Shugendō flourished at Mount Daisen, with {{ill|Tiantai|en|Tiantai|qid=Q668188|lt=Tendai Buddhism}} becoming dominant. At its peak between the late Heian and Muromachi periods, Daisen-ji oversaw over 160 temples and shrines and boasted an army of 3,000 {{ill|Sōhei|en|Sōhei|qid=Q1475695|lt=warrior monks}}.<ref>[http://yokoso.pref.tottori.jp/dd.aspx?itemid=1705 Tottori Prefecture Tourism Information - Daisen-ji]</ref>
During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, Chimyō Gongen (associated with Jizō Bosatsu), Reizō Gongen (associated with Kannon Bosatsu), and Riju Gongen (associated with Monju Bosatsu) formed the '''{{ill|Three Deities of Mount Daisen|ja|大山三所権現|qid=Q140446061}}'''.<ref>According to the Daisen-ji Engi, Monju, Kannon, and Jizō Bosatsu manifested with Sanskrit characters, seated west, east, and center respectively, forming the Three Deities of Daisen.</ref>
== Pilgrimage to Mount Daisen ==
The belief that Mount Daisen was a resting place for souls of the deceased led to the fusion of Daisen worship and Jizō devotion. Pilgrimages to pray for the repose of the dead at Chimyō Gongen flourished during the Edo period. Today, the {{ill|33 Kannon Pilgrimage of Daisen-ji|ja|大山寺三十三カ所地蔵めぐり|qid=Q140446062}} route reflects these historical practices.
== Shinbutsu Bunri and Haibutsu Kishaku ==
The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}-era {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離令|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535}} led to the abolition of Shugendō-related deities like Chimyō Gongen. In 1871 (Meiji 4), Daisen-ji was forcibly separated into {{ill|Ōgamiyama Shrine|en|Ōgamiyama Shrine|qid=Q251160|lt=Ōgamiyama Shrine}} and the Tendai sect temple Kakuban-san Daisen-ji.
== Temples Enshrining Chimyō Gongen ==
Though few, some temples continue to enshrine Chimyō Gongen, having survived the anti-Buddhist purges:
* {{ill|Kakuban-san Daisen-ji Temple|ja|角磐山大山寺|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135550942}}<ref>[http://www.daisenji.jp/ Official Site of Kakuban-san Daisen-ji]</ref><ref>10th temple of the {{ill|Izumo Shinbutsu Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11395860}}</ref> ({{ill|Tottori Prefecture|en|Tottori Prefecture|qid=Q133935|lt=Tottori Prefecture}}, Saihaku District)
* {{ill|Ōgashima-ji Temple|ja|大賀島寺|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11439240}}, Daitōzan ({{ill|Setouchi, Okayama|en|Setouchi, Okayama|qid=Q691691|lt=Setouchi, Okayama}}) - Spring Festival for Daichimyō Daigongen
* {{ill|Kaizō-ji Temple|ja|海蔵寺|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11559209}}, Busshōzan ({{ill|Kasaoka|en|Kasaoka|qid=Q863739|lt=Kasaoka, Okayama}})<ref>10th temple of the {{ill|Chugoku Kannon Pilgrimage|ja|中国観音霊場|qid=Q140447353}}</ref><ref>[http://www.city.kasaoka.okayama.jp/001p/001q.html Official Kasaoka City Website]</ref>
* {{ill|Senkoji|ja|千光寺|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11405368}}, Daihōzan ({{ill|Onomichi|en|Onomichi|qid=Q696694|lt=Onomichi, Hiroshima}})<ref>[http://www.senkouji.jp/guidance/info011.html Senkō-ji Official Site]</ref>
* {{ill|Goryū Sontakuin|ja|五流尊瀧院|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11372540}} ({{ill|Kurashiki|en|Kurashiki|qid=Q467487|lt=Kurashiki, Okayama}}) - Daisen Chimyō Daigongen
